title: छन्द अनुशीलन {Rhyme practice}
nepali: समस्त वेदका ऋचा छन्दमा संरचित छन् । आचार्य पिङ्गलले वेदमा उल्लिखित छन्दहरू र पूर्वलक्षणकारकाअभिमतलाई समेत समेटेर छन्दःसूत्रम् तयार पारे । प्रस्तुत छन्दःसूत्रम्लाई मूल आधार बनाएर लेखिएका श्रुतबोध,छन्दःशास्त्रम्, वृत्तरत्नाकर, मन्दारमरन्दचम्पू, वृत्तचन्द्रिका आदि लक्षण ग्रन्थहरूले शास्त्रीय छन्दको विकास रविस्तारमा ठोस योगदान पु¥याएका छन् । उत्तरवैदिककाल, लौकिककाल, प्राकृतकाल हुँदै विकसित आधुनिककालीननेपाली, हिन्दी आदि भाषाहरूमा समेत शास्त्रीय छन्दहरूको उपयोग गरी विश्वविख्यात सुन्दर काव्यहरू सृजनागरिएका छन् । विद्यालय र महाविद्यालयहरूको पाठ्यक्रममा समेत शास्त्रीय छन्दलाई समावेश गरिएको परिस्थितिमाशास्त्रीय छन्दको व्युत्पत्तिसहित परिचय दिनु, यसका तत्त्व, गण देवता र गणअनुसारका शुभ अशुभ फल उल्लेखगर्नु, शास्त्रीय छन्दका प्रकार उल्लेख गर्नु र तिनका प्रतिनिधिमूलक रूपमा एकएक ओटा लक्षण र तिनको उदाहरणप्रस्तुत गर्नु यस लेखको उद्देश्य रहेको छ । गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान ढाँचामा आधारित रही उद्देश्यमूलक नमुना छनोटप्रक्रिया अवलम्बन गरिएको यस लेखमा पुस्तकालयीय विधि उपयोग गरिएको छ । यसमा पूर्वीय वाङ्मयकोआद्यादर्श ग्रन्थ वेद शास्त्रीय छन्दमा रचना गरिएको तथ्य प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । छन्दको व्युत्पत्ति, अर्थ, यसकातत्त्वहरू, गण, गणदेवता र गणका शुभ र अशुभ फल निरूपण गरिएको छ । छन्दमा कविता काव्य सृजना गर्दाअनुसरण गर्नुपर्ने र गर्न मिल्नेसम्मका नियम उदाहरणसहित उल्लेख गरिएको छ । शास्त्रीय छन्दको वार्णिक भेदकासमवृत्तअन्तर्गत साधारण भेदका एकअक्षरीय उक्थादेखि २६ अक्षरीय उत्कृतिसम्म, अद्र्धसमवृत्त, विषमवृत्त, मात्रिकछन्दअन्तर्गत सम, अद्र्धसम र विषममात्रिक छन्दका प्रतिनिधिमूलक रूपमा एकएक लक्षण र विभिन्न काव्यमा रहेकाउदाहरण प्रस्तुत गरी नेपाली काव्यमा छन्द प्रयोगको अवस्थालाई देखाइएको छ । {All the Vedas are structured in rich verses. Acharya Pingal prepared the verses by including the verses mentioned in the Vedas and the opinion of the forerunner. Srutabodh, Chhandashastram, Vrittaratnakar, Mandaramarandachampu, Vrittachandrika, etc., written on the basis of the present Chhandasutram, have made a significant contribution to the development of classical verse. The world famous beautiful poems have been created using classical verses even in the modern Nepali, Hindi and other languages ​​developed through the post-Vedic period, secular period and natural period. The purpose of this article is to introduce classical verse in the curriculum of schools and colleges with the origin of classical verse. Based on a qualitative research framework, an objective sample selection process has been adopted. This article uses the library method. It presents the fact that the ideal text of Eastern literature is composed in Vedic classical verse. The etymology of the verse, its meaning, its elements, Gana, Ganadevata and the auspicious and inauspicious fruits of Gana are described. When creating poetry in verse, the rules to be followed and what can be done are mentioned with examples. From the monosyllabic utterances of the common distinctions to the 26-syllable utterances of the classical verses under the chromatic distinction of the classical verses, the semiotic, heterogeneous, even, symmetrical and heterogeneous verses under the metrical verses are represented in each of the verses and examples in various poems.}
american_english: The verses (richas) of all the Vedas are structured in meter. Acharya Pingala prepared the Chandahsutram by synthesizing the meters mentioned in the Vedas and also the views of predecessor prosodists. Treatises on metrics written taking this Chandahsutram as the primary foundation—such as Shrutabodha, Chandahshastram, Vrittaratnakara, Mandaramarandachampu, Vrittachandrika, and others—have made concrete contributions to the development and expansion of classical meter. World-renowned beautiful poetic works have been created utilizing classical meters even in modern-period languages such as Nepali, Hindi, and others that developed through the post-Vedic period, classical Sanskrit period, and Prakrit period. In a context where classical meter has been incorporated into the curricula of schools and colleges, the objective of this article is to introduce classical meter along with its etymology, to state its elements, ganas (metrical feet), deities of the ganas, and the auspicious and inauspicious fruits according to the ganas, to mention the types of classical meter, and to present one characteristic definition and one example for each as representative models. Based on a qualitative research framework and adopting a purposive sampling process, a library method has been utilized in this article. In this, the fact that the primordial exemplary text of Eastern literature, the Vedas, was composed in classical meter is presented. The etymology, meaning, and elements of meter, ganas, deities of ganas, and auspicious and inauspicious fruits of ganas have been delineated. The rules that must be followed and can be observed when composing poetry and poetic works in meter have been mentioned with examples. By presenting, as representative models, one characteristic definition and examples found in various poetic works from the one-syllable uktha to the 26-syllable utkriti under ordinary varieties of syllabic samavritta in classical meter, as well as ardhasamavritta, vishamavritta, and moraic meters including sama, ardhasama, and vishamamatrika meters, the state of meter usage in Nepali poetry has been demonstrated.

Acharya Pingala put together the Chandahsutram by gathering the meters mentioned in the Vedas along with the views of earlier prosody scholars. Treatises on poetic rules written off the back of this Chandahsutram—like Shrutabodha, Chandahshastram, Vrittaratnakara, Mandaramarandachampu, Vrittachandrika, and others—have made a solid, concrete contribution to developing and expanding classical meter. World-renowned beautiful poetic works have been crafted using classical meters even in modern-period tongues like Nepali, Hindi, and others that developed through the post-Vedic, classical Sanskrit, and Prakrit periods. With classical meter being taught in schools and colleges these days, the whole point of this article is to introduce classical meter along with its etymology, lay out its elements, the ganas (metrical feet), deities of the ganas, and the lucky or unlucky outcomes that come with them, outline the types of classical meter, and dish out representative definitions and examples for each. Built on a qualitative research framework and using a purposive sampling process, this article uses library methods. Right here, the fact that the primordial exemplary text of Eastern literature, the Vedas, was composed in classical meter is presented. The etymology, meaning, and elements of meter, ganas, deities of ganas, and the auspicious and inauspicious fruits of ganas are all sorted out. The rules you have to follow and what you can get away with when making poetry in meter have been laid out with examples. And by dishing out representative definitions and examples from various poems—all the way from the single-syllable uktha up to the 26-syllable utkriti under ordinary varieties of syllabic samavritta in classical meter, through ardhasamavritta, vishamavritta, and moraic meters including sama, ardhasama, and vishamamatrika meters—the state of meter usage in Nepali poetry has been clearly shown.
